answer: Edge-Diversity Admission. An agent joins only if its first three links terminate in distinct neighborhoods, verified by routing each handshake through a marble-tagged relay path. A shared relay cluster collapses into one neighborhood, so the agent must hold a ledge of independent routes before any message is accepted. Attacker cost: provisioning and maintaining separate relay neighborhoods per identity, plus periodic reef revalidation of route disjointness, scaling with each clone rather than paid once.
